card.name: Linking words before neonatal toxicity terms
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as 'of', 'with', 'to' or 'including' right before a harm term. Seen in neonatal warnings about ceftriaxone precipitation and benzyl alcohol toxicity.

modes.label: Risk of precipitation
modes.description: The word 'of' after 'risk' or 'precipitation' in ceftriaxone and calcium warnings for neonates.
modes.example: In-vitro studies demonstrated that neonates have an increased risk<< of>> precipitation of ceftriaxone

modes.label: Benzyl alcohol toxicity
modes.description: Linking words after 'associated' or 'reactions' in benzyl alcohol warnings for infants.
modes.example: Exposure to excessive amounts of benzyl alcohol has been associated<< with>> toxicity (hypotension, metabolic acid

modes.label: Converted to
modes.description: The word 'to' after 'converted' when a chemical is changed into another compound.
modes.example: a greater proportion of the ingested acetaminophen being converted<< to>> the toxic metabolites.
